_meta.note: All statistics computed directly from M1 clean CSVs — raw sensor units preserved throughout. No transformation between M1 and M2.

column_suffix_meanings._mean: Arithmetic mean of all samples in cluster

normalization_usage.P_star: P* = P_actual / P_cluster_mean  (pressure and vibration channels)
normalization_usage.T_ambient_source: Temperature column (ambient air, degC) — per-row value, NOT fixed 20.0 degC
normalization_usage.normal_range: Normal operation -> normalised values approximately 0 to 1. Fault -> drift above 1.0

physics_paradox_note.description: K-Means Thermal Run-In Paradox — documented for audit trail
physics_paradox_note.observation: Startup cluster (C2) mean Mot.TV=39.61 degC > High-load cluster (C3) mean Mot.TV=35.09 degC
physics_paradox_note.engineering_explanation: Pump starts cold. First minutes of startup: bearings heat rapidly from near-ambient to 39+ degC while flow/pressure is still ramping up. High-load steady operation: bearings settle at 35 degC with turbulent cooling from high volumetric flow. This is physically correct and matches industrial pump thermal behaviour.
physics_paradox_note.consequence_for_ML: Temperature channels are CORROBORATING only. Vibration (SV) and pressure (Pres.SV) are primary discriminators. Fault rules in M5/M6 use rate-of-change dX*/dt, not absolute cluster temperature comparisons.
